- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 68.02 → 69.64 in Example 1).
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting mean reversion or lagged response.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when history includes recent high prices.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum after strong upward moves; often holds high values longer than true price declines.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) but become more accurate later (5–10 days), suggesting a lag in adjusting to recent trends.
- When history includes a sharp decline, model often fails to reflect it, continuing to project upward or flat trends.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts rise with recent price peaks but don’t adjust for subsequent corrections.
- Forecasts are less accurate when history includes a prolonged downtrend — model tends to underestimate the depth of the decline.
- Model does not account for seasonal or calendar-based patterns (e.g., end-of-month or quarter effects) in price behavior.
